summary:
FIELD SHIFT is an interactive agricultural intelligence platform designed to transform Earth observation and climate data into meaningful insights for more climate-resilient agriculture.

Developed with a focus on Kazakhstan and other climate-sensitive agricultural regions, the platform brings together geographical exploration, NASA climate data, satellite imagery, and agricultural decision-support tools in one digital workspace.

Its capabilities include a Field Digital Twin, Earth Pulse Profiles, Climate Time Machine, Satellite Date Comparison, Crop Rotation Intelligence, Impact Analyzer, and Early Warning. Together, these tools help users explore environmental conditions, investigate changes over time, and understand potential agricultural risks.

By integrating NASA POWER climate indicators with interactive visualisation and location-based analysis, FIELD SHIFT makes complex environmental information more accessible and easier to interpret.

Our goal is to bridge the gap between Earth science and real-world agricultural decision-making, helping build a future where farmers and communities can make more informed decisions in a changing climate.
details:
FIELD SHIFT — An Integrated Agricultural Intelligence Platform

1. Project Overview

FIELD SHIFT is an interactive web platform designed to connect Earth observation, climate intelligence, geographical analysis, and agricultural decision support.

The project addresses a growing challenge: agricultural decisions are increasingly influenced by environmental variability, yet relevant scientific information is often distributed across separate tools and presented in formats that are difficult for non-specialists to interpret.

Our solution is to bring these different perspectives together in one accessible digital environment.

2. How It Works

FIELD SHIFT follows a connected analytical workflow:

Explore → Observe → Compare → Analyse → Understand

Users begin by exploring a geographical area through an interactive map. They can then investigate available environmental indicators, examine satellite imagery, compare observations across different dates, and explore agricultural implications.

The platform is organised into interconnected modules:

FIELD DIGITAL TWIN

Provides an interactive geographical environment for exploring selected locations and their environmental context.

SOIL INTELLIGENCE

Creates an agricultural analysis environment focused on soil-related information, land characteristics, and sustainability considerations.

EARTH PULSE PROFILES

Transforms climate indicators into accessible location-based environmental profiles.

CLIMATE TIME MACHINE

Supports the exploration of historical climate conditions and changes in environmental indicators over time.

SATELLITE DATE COMPARISON

Allows users to examine satellite imagery from different dates and investigate visible changes in selected geographical areas.

CROP ROTATION INTELLIGENCE

Provides an exploratory framework for investigating crop rotation considerations and environmental factors relevant to agricultural planning.

IMPACT ANALYZER

Organises environmental information into an agricultural impact analysis framework.

EARLY WARNING

Aims to highlight potentially concerning environmental conditions and improve awareness of possible agricultural risks.

WHAT-IF SCENARIOS

Provides a framework for exploring hypothetical environmental conditions and considering their possible implications for agricultural decisions.

3. NASA Data Integration

An important foundation of FIELD SHIFT is NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources).

The platform uses or explores NASA POWER environmental indicators, including temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation.

These indicators help users investigate the environmental context of agricultural locations.

The project is designed to make scientific datasets more accessible through interactive maps, visualisations, and location-based exploration.

4. Technology and Development

FIELD SHIFT was developed as a web-based application using Replit.

The development process involved:

  • Front-end development and interactive user interface design.
  • Geographical visualisation and map integration.
  • Integration of external climate data services.
  • Interactive analytical modules.
  • Data presentation and visualisation.
  • Testing, debugging, and iterative improvements.

Technologies and resources include NASA POWER API, OpenStreetMap, Esri mapping services, Replit, and AI-assisted development tools.

5. Creativity and Innovation

The main creative aspect of FIELD SHIFT is its integrated architecture.

Instead of presenting climate indicators, geographical information, satellite imagery, and agricultural tools as isolated features, the project connects them through a unified workspace.

Its design combines three important dimensions:

  • Spatial intelligence: where environmental conditions occur.
  • Temporal intelligence: how environmental conditions change.
  • Agricultural intelligence: why those changes may matter for farming.

This creates a foundation for a more connected approach to understanding agricultural vulnerability.

6. Intended Impact

FIELD SHIFT aims to:

  • Improve access to Earth observation and climate information.
  • Support environmental awareness in agricultural communities.
  • Help users investigate historical and changing climate conditions.
  • Encourage more informed agricultural planning.
  • Make scientific information easier to understand through interactive technology.

Kazakhstan provides an important initial context for the project because understanding climate variability is particularly relevant to agricultural regions.

7. Future Potential

FIELD SHIFT is designed as an expandable platform.

Future development could include more detailed soil datasets, validated crop suitability models, improved environmental risk assessment, and additional satellite data sources.

Our long-term vision is to transform complex environmental information into practical agricultural intelligence.

FIELD SHIFT — Turning Earth’s data into tomorrow’s decisions.
